vefur-sync.summary: Yes to both. (1) If ㊵ deletes a retired <basename>_IS.svg from every efni publication track that holds it, the next vefur sync of efnafraedi-2e removes it from static/content. The mt-preview baseline is mirrored with `rsync -av --delete --delete-excluded` (vefur scripts/sync-content.js:311), and faithful is then copied on top with no deletion (cpSync force:true, :411). I measured this with byte-identical copies of vefur's own scripts against a scratch fixture: a file deleted from mt-preview disappeared, but a file deleted from mt-preview and still present in faithful came back with faithful's bytes, even though rsync printed `deleting …` for it. The deletion then reaches the server: `npm run build` empties build/ first (adapter-static index.js:62-63), both deploy routes run rsync with --delete (docs/guides/deployment.md:89 for manual, .github/workflows/deploy.yml:110 for CI), and efnafraedi-2e is in neither exclude list. I measured that list over the real efni tree: downloads/, edlisfraedi-2e/, liffraedi-2e/, orverufraedi/. (2) If efni keeps the file and only stops referencing it, it stays deployed and can be fetched by URL. Nothing in the sync, build or deploy prunes by reference: the prune step touches .html only, and the validator and audit never look at images. That held in the fixture (an unreferenced file survived four runs) and on real data: each of the ten has its original .jpg in the same published directory, referenced by 0 of 265 HTML files, and the .jpg is in vefur's local static/content and build/content. The two tracks are flattened into one static/content/<book>/. Faithful wins every name clash except chapter-rollup .html pages and the book glossary/index.json, which are gated, so an image always gets faithful's bytes (measured). That matters for ibuprofenmass_img: both tracks' 3-1 pages reference one absolute URL. The stale-directory sweep is keyed on the efni SOURCE tree's book list (availableBooks, :752) and only removes whole top-level book directories, never chapters or images (measured: a ghost book was removed and a withheld book was kept). static/content is gitignored (.gitignore:35; 0 tracked files, against 21 tracked under static/). Four caveats. The local sync reads the efni working tree at ../namsbokasafn-efni, which is currently on feat/c140-c40-retire-and-alias. A bare sync today also selects lifraen-efnafraedi. `--dry-run` runs only the baseline mirror, so its `deleting` lines over-report. The /downloads PDFs are outside --delete and keep retired figures until regenerated by hand. `git status --porcelain` is empty in both repos. Porcelain cannot see the gitignored static/content and build/, so the evidence that nothing was written is a `find -newer` check: 0 hits in vefur static/, build/ and scripts/ and in efni's chemistry 05-publication, against a control of 6 scratch files that it did catch.

designImplications: RETIRE must delete the 05-publication/<track>/chapters/NN/images/media/<basename>_IS.svg copy in EVERY track that holds it. For the six retirees that is the mt-preview copy only. A copy left in place and merely unreferenced stays synced, built and deployed, reachable at its absolute /content/… URL, with no end date.

Deleting only the mt-preview copy of a file that faithful also holds does nothing for readers: the overlay puts it back. The tool should list the copies across both tracks rather than assume mt-preview.

ibuprofenmass_img (the override recompose): the new SVG must reach faithful/chapters/03, by re-rendering faithful ch03 or both tracks. Both 3-1 pages reference one URL and faithful's bytes win, so updating mt-preview alone changes nothing a reader gets.

Inferred: a recompose written to the SAME filename does not bust caches. Returning PWA readers whose service worker cached the June SVG can keep seeing it for up to 30 days (CacheFirst, 200-entry LRU). This applies to all four recomposes; whether to change the name is the controller's decision.
Do not take `sync-content.js --dry-run` as proof of a retirement. It shows only the baseline mirror, and its 'deleting' lines over-report. Check the tree after a real sync, or the deployed file.

Post-deploy check: fetch /content/efnafraedi-2e/chapters/NN/images/media/<basename>_IS.svg and expect 404, alongside a nonsense .svg in the same directory (also 404) and a kept SVG (200, real bytes). The original .jpg the page falls back to should return 200. A uniformly clean set proves nothing without these controls.

The sync that publishes ㊵ must name the book (`sync-content.js efnafraedi-2e`), because a bare run also selects organic. efni must be on the intended branch at that moment, because the sync reads its working tree.
/downloads/efnafraedi-2e/*.pdf are outside --delete and refreshed only by hand (`npm run pdfs` plus a separate rsync). For PDF readers, a retirement or recompose is not finished until that refresh.

vefur has no check that an resolves. If a page still referenced a deleted SVG, every vefur gate would stay green and readers would get a broken image. The re-render that drops the reference has to happen with the deletion, and any 'no HTML references it' check must run on the efni side.

Inject builds every module fresh from 01-source and then rewrites the image name as a separate final step, using image-mapping.json rows keyed on the image basename (cnxml-inject.js:5482-5503, 1188-1212). If a row is removed, the original `../../media/.jpg` and `image/jpeg` come back. A pure probe of that rewrite step shows this for all 10, and commit 8ebdf1a4f (Ques11ans, 2026-09-19) shows it on a full inject run. No path in inject or render picks up an _IS file because it sits in media/. The only presence-based producer is generate-image-mapping.js, which nothing runs automatically. Render takes the src from 03-translated, writes `/content//chapters//images/media/`, and then copies only the files the chapter's HTML references, looking first in 01-source/media and then in media/. Every _IS file comes from media/. Render never deletes anything under images/media/, so a retired figure's published SVG stays behind: the 8 June `_reverted/` SVGs and one GasBurning SVG are already sitting there unreferenced. On the server side, an image is served only when the figure has a sidecar, a mapping row, and the file on disk; nothing goes by file presence alone.

designImplications: A retire must remove BOTH the mapping row and books/efnafraedi-2e/media/<b>_IS.svg. Removing only the row lets the next generate-image-mapping run add it back (it scans the top level of media/). Removing only the file leaves inject swapping to _IS.svg; render then warns 'Referenced image not found in source' and keeps serving the stale published copy. Moving the SVG into the existing gitignored media/_reverted/ also prevents the re-add, because the scan is non-recursive. That is the June convention, where 146 files sit; the §C163 precedent deleted the file outright instead.

Deleting the published copy is a separate, explicit step: no render path ever deletes under 05-publication/<track>/chapters/NN/images/media/. The §C163 precedent deleted it by hand. resolver-contract.summary: figure-run.js spawns `sources.py --json <book> <names...>` once per pass (tools/figure-run.js:522-546). A non-zero exit aborts the whole run; otherwise each entry is read as a hit if it has a truthy `path`, as a refusal if it has a truthy `refused`, and as a hole if it is null. From a hit the driver reads only `path`, `edition` and `pageUnknown` (:2008-2018, :2047-2057). There is no switch over refusal kinds: any truthy `refused` becomes outcome `unresolved`, which is not fatal. An unknown kind gets a generic `rec.reason`, but the printed REFUSED line still shows its `reason`. The resolved path is used for exactly four things: the prepare argv, a truthiness check in the classifier, the one-artwork-one-figure backstop key, and a report line printed only for de-hashed figures. `rec.edition` is written and never read anywhere. figure-prepare.py stages every artwork as `<out>/<basename>.pdf`, so no stage takes a name from the artwork's own filename. Sidecars record no artwork path, edition or hash (459 of 459), `isStale` checks hashes only, and a current sidecar is skipped before anything is resolved. conventions.summary: Nothing in the repo forces one shape on a new destructive CLI, but the precedents agree on most of it. (1) tools/__tests__/generate-image-mapping.test.js builds no fixtures at all. It tests only the pure core with inline CNXML strings and in-memory arrays, and pins DEFAULT_SUFFIX by reading the committed chemistry mapping (non-vacuity is a length check above 100). `_setTestBooksDir` is exported but no test uses it, so `generateImageMapping()`'s file-handling half has no test. The tmp-dir idioms live in other tests: export-corpus and generate-tm use a module-global seam, and figure-run-paid builds `books/<slug>/01-source` plus `media/` under `mkdtemp` and passes in `booksRoot`. (2) Every script that DELETES or rewrites committed data defaults to a dry run and needs `--apply`, `--db` or `--execute`: remove-wrong-sense-headwords (verified), repair-invented-markers, backfill-appendix-sections, reattach-segment-edits and fetch-bin-inflections. The figure-track producers (generate-image-mapping, normalize-svg-dimensions, publish-figure-svg, figure-run) write by default. (3) Both tools/lib/parseArgs.js and generate-image-mapping's own parser silently drop unknown flags. I measured `--dryrun` WRITING through generate-image-mapping, and `--apply=false` coming back as `apply:true` through parseArgs. Only figure-run.js's parser refuses unknown flags inside tools/, and its test pins that. No test pins any tool's flag list. (4) Usage errors exit 2; set `process.exitCode` and `return` rather than calling `process.exit` after output. The main guard most tools use is `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`. (5) No tool that writes into media/ or 05-publication leaves a `.bak`; git is the restore, and the publication pruner writes a record instead. A `.bak` in `chapters/NN/images/media/` would not be swept by cnxml-render (it only clears the top level of the chapter folder), would not be committed (`*.bak` is gitignored) and would not reach vefur (its rsync excludes it; I measured this). (6) docs/workflow says nothing about figures. The places to document are the tool's header and its `--help` text, the generated docs/_generated/tools.md (CI's docs-check fails if it is not regenerated), the figure-text README, the config's `_key` notes, the sources.py comments, REGISTER.md provenance, the §C140 ㊵ row, and two stale texts the ㊵ PR should fix. (7) LICENSE does not forbid a tools/ script from loading server/ code, but every such link has to be listed in LICENSE; generate-image-mapping.js has none today. Biggest surprise: the publication tree holds 12 more `_IS.svg` copies with the same older TrueType fonts, which are not among the 10. Nine of them are June leftovers that no page uses and that have survived every re-render since. That is exactly what a retire that skips 05-publication leaves behind.
